conviction_note: The negative lean comes from public mortgage-rate and application data. The 30y rate went from about 6.6% when the July guide was set to 7.4% by 15 Oct, and refi applications were 19-56% below a year earlier through Aug-Sep, against a Q3 guide that assumed originations down low single digits. That points to a Q3 mortgage shortfall and a likely Q4/FY guide cut. Pushing back toward 50: the skew already pays for downside, the sell-side has cut targets six times this month, EFX has beaten EPS four quarters running with cost levers, and a bi-merge reprieve rally can carry. So p_up is 42 on an abs move of 7.5, giving -1.2. The findings sum to -2.8 because each is sized on its own and not fitted to the scaled number; the gap is the partly-priced discount.
bar: Q3 2026: revenue $1.69bn, adj EPS $2.20 (Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-10-15, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stay-ahead-game-equifax-efx-121523086.html). That agrees with the company guide of $1.68-1.71bn / $2.15-2.25 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000033185/000003318526000024/exhibit99120260630.htm) and with $2.21 EPS / $1.69bn from Earnings Whispers / Alphastreet. FY2026 guide is $8.39-8.69 adj EPS (mid $8.54); FY consensus is $8.53 (MarketBeat 2026-10-19, single source, possibly stale), which implies a Q4 bar of about $2.22 (8.53 - 1.86 Q1 - 2.25 Q2 - 2.20 Q3). Segment bars (Zacks): EWS $703.7m, USIS $600.6m, International $388.2m. Q3 guide internals from the Q2 call: US mortgage revenue up about 20%, originations down low single digits.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 5.9% of float, 3.1 days to cover (Equibles, snapshot ~2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/EFX), and 6.6M shares, 4.62 days to cover at the 2026-07-15 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/efx/short-interest/). Moderate, not a crowded short. Skew is +2.58 vol points, put/call OI 1.95, event-implied move 7.16%, priced lean 'downside paid'. Spot $159.69: +8.4% over 5 sessions (an 11-12% bounce off ~$143-146 in early October on the 15 Oct sector rally after FHFA did not announce bi-merge at MBA Annual), +0.7% over 20 days, -31.7% from the 52-week high, ~-33% YTD.

findings.finding: MBA weekly data show the Q3 mortgage market weakening well beyond the July guide. Week ending 7 Aug: refi -22% and purchase -1% YoY. Week ending 28 Aug: refi -19%, purchase ~0%. Week ending 25 Sep: refi -56% and purchase -14% YoY, with the 30y at 7.3%. Equifax's Q3 guide assumed originations down only low single digits and US mortgage revenue up about 20%, so Q3 mortgage inquiries (and the ~25% of revenue that is US mortgage) likely land below the guide's assumption, against a Q3 2025 base boosted by a September 2025 refi spike.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2023: mortgage inquiries fell 29% vs a -23% guide and the stock fell ~6% on the FY cut. Q3 2025: inquiries -7% vs a feared -12% and the stock moved only -0.51%. Q1 2026 beat on mortgage (+38%) but fell -3.04%. This name has not paid for reported-quarter mortgage beats, but it has sold off on mortgage misses that carry into the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 EPS consensus has moved only -0.9% in 30 days ($2.23 to $2.20) and still sits at the guide midpoint, and revenue consensus ($1.69bn) is at the midpoint too. If the market had priced a mortgage shortfall, Q3 estimates would sit at the low end of the $2.15-2.25 range.
findings.independence: August data come from a different document, HousingWire 2026-08-12 (refi -22% YoY, purchase -1%): https://www.housingwire.com/articles/mortgage-applications-climb/. Guide assumption from the Q2 call transcript: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-equifax-beats-q2-2026-eps-but-shares-fall-93CH-4803756. Proxy: MBA applications are not Equifax hard inquiries, and Equifax usually outgrows the market on pricing and share.

findings.finding: The 30y mortgage rate was 7.4% on 15 Oct 2026 (highest since Nov 2023), against roughly 6.6% embedded in the July FY guide (management: 'current mortgage rates are what is embedded'). Q4 2025 had a refi-heavy base at ~6.2-6.3%, so the implied Q4 guide (~$2.23 adj EPS at the FY midpoint, and ~$2.22 in FY consensus of $8.53) is likely cut when Equifax gives its Q4 outlook on 20 Oct.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide-driven: Q2 2025 -8.18% on the outlook; Q2 2026 -3.93% (about -7% intraday per the sweep) on a below-consensus Q3 guide despite an EPS beat; Oct 2023 about -6% on a mortgage-driven FY cut. Five of seven prints in the baseline fell.
findings.why_not_priced: FY consensus ($8.53, MarketBeat 2026-10-19) still sits at the FY guide midpoint ($8.54) despite an ~80bp rate rise since the guide. Price-target cuts (RBC citing higher rates) suggest the buy-side expects some cut, but the bounce to $160 on bi-merge relief means the price is no longer at its early-October low. Partly priced: the skew pays for downside.
findings.independence: Rate path from Freddie Mac PMMS (6.71% on 3 Sep, 7.28% on 1 Oct) via a separate series: https://freddiemac.gcs-web.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mortgage-rates-average-671. Embedded-rate comment from Yahoo's Q2 call highlights: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/equifax-q2-earnings-call-highlights-150701435.html. Shares the macro driver (rates) with finding 1 but lands on a different line (Q4/FY guide, not Q3 actuals).

findings.finding: US hiring is weakening into the quarter. September payrolls were +29k vs ~90k expected, July was revised to -10k and August cut to +133k, and unemployment rose to 4.2%. That weighs on EWS Talent Solutions (already declining in Q2) and non-mortgage verification volumes, against a Q3 guide for diversified markets up mid-single digits.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2024/Q4 2024: hiring weakness in EWS Talent was repeatedly cited in guide trims; there is no clean isolated reaction in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Public macro print, and the Talent decline was already known in Q2, so this is mostly priced. Its residual value is whether management extends the weakness into the Q4 guide.
findings.independence: BLS TED note: https://www.bls.gov/opub/ted/2026/nonfarm-employment-little-changed-in-september-2026.htm. Proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by Equifax.

findings.finding: The +8.4% five-session run-up is a sector relief rally (TRU +10.7%, Experian +7%, EFX +7.25% on 15 Oct) after FHFA Director Pulte skipped MBA Annual without the expected tri-merge to bi-merge announcement. The overhang stays open: MBA's CEO said he is 'increasingly confident that tri-merge won't be around for long'. So EFX goes into the print 11-12% off its early-October low with no company news behind the bounce.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EFX fell ~4% on 29 Sep (unified VantageScore grid) and ~4% the week of 1 Oct (Bloomberg bi-merge report), then gained 7.25% on 15 Oct. Regulatory headlines move it 4-7% in a day.
findings.why_not_priced: The bounce is in the price by definition. What is not priced is whether the call's bi-merge questions and a mortgage guide cut give the relief back. If management quantifies bi-merge exposure as small (William Blair: ~$270m tri-merge-linked revenue, low-to-mid single digit EBITDA if a third is lost), the sign flips, hence the wide high band.
findings.independence: GuruFocus on the 15 Oct sector rally: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9126375/transunion-tru-surges-over-10-amid-sector-rally-highlighting-undervalued-status. William Blair estimate via Investing.com 2026-10-02: https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/equifax-and-transunion-shares-fall-on-mortgage-credit-report-rule-change-93CH-4864411.

findings.finding: On 29 Sep 2026 FHFA put VantageScore 4.0 on the same LLPA grid as Classic FICO. The bureaus priced VantageScore at about $1 (TRU at $0.99 through Dec 2028), and TRU said VantageScore was already in ~30% of its mortgage inquiries by Q2. Equifax's 2026 guide assumes it keeps selling FICO scores for all 2026 mortgage transactions, with limited VantageScore revenue, so any lender switching in Q4 lowers reported mortgage revenue (FICO pass-through) and muddies the Q4/2027 outlook.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EFX fell 4.1% pre-market (closed -3%) on the 29 Sep grid announcement. The FICO direct-license news in Oct 2025 also hit the bureaus.
findings.why_not_priced: The headline is priced (-3% that day). What is not is Equifax's first quantification of Q4 FICO/VantageScore mix in its own guide. FICO revenue is low-margin pass-through, so the EPS impact is smaller than the revenue impact; sized small.
findings.independence: TRU Q2 2026 call (VantageScore ~30% of TRU mortgage inquiries): https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8984017/transunion-tru-q2-2026-earnings-call-highlights-strong-revenue-growth-and-raised-fullyear-guidance. FICO-assumption wording: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/equifax-q2-earnings-call-highlights-150701435.html

findings.finding: EWS government verification was guided to return to growth in 2H 2026, with ~$300M of new annual contract value signed (mostly a 2027 benefit, some in 2H26) and a pipeline about 2x the year-ago level. Medicaid/SNAP work requirements from Jan 2027 give Equifax room to talk up 2027 on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Government verification was the swing line in 2025 prints (Q2 2025 -8.18% partly on a government slowdown). No clean positive reaction on this line in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly inside the company's own guide, so near zero. The residual is a 2027 framework mention that offsets mortgage gloom; Senate scrutiny (Warren/Wyden/Sanders, Feb 2026) caps how much the market pays for it.
findings.independence: Senate investigation on Work Number pricing and work requirements: https://www.warren.senate.gov/newsroom/press-releases/warren-wyden-sanders-announce-new-investigation-into-equifaxs-plan-to-profit-from-trumps-so-called-work-requirements-in-medicaid-snap

findings.finding: Equifax has beaten consensus EPS four quarters running (avg ~5%), and Q2 2026 came in $0.05 above the guide midpoint. It doubled its AI-driven cost-reduction target to $150m (2026 savings in guide), giving a cost lever to hold Q3 EPS near $2.20 even with a mortgage revenue shortfall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats are sold: Q1 2026 beat by ~10% ($1.86 vs ~$1.70) and the stock fell -3.04%; Q2 2026 beat by $0.05 and it fell -3.93%.
findings.why_not_priced: Beat cadence is well known and the name has not paid for beats. Sized small because the reaction function vetoes it.
findings.independence: Zacks beat history via Yahoo preview: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stay-ahead-game-equifax-efx-121523086.html

findings.finding: Six price-target cuts cluster in 2-19 Oct 2026, ahead of the print: Barclays 200 to 155 (EW, citing negative sector sentiment), Goldman 171 to 148 (Neutral), BofA 210 to 200, Morgan Stanley 225 to 205, RBC 194 to 177 (higher rates, consumer lending, credit-reporting rule risk), Mizuho 210 to 185 on 19 Oct. That lowers the sentiment bar into a guide cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025 print (Feb 2026, +3.42%) came after a heavy de-rating; reaction history after pre-print PT-cut clusters is not isolated in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Targets moved, but EPS estimates barely did (-0.9% in 30 days for Q3; FY $8.53 at the guide midpoint), so the multiple has been reset more than the numbers. That partly offsets finding 2: a moderate guide cut may already be expected by the buy-side.
findings.independence: Barclays cut via StockStory 2026-10-02: https://www.financialcontent.com/article/stockstory-2026-10-2-equifax-efx-stock-trades-up-here-is-why. RBC/BofA/GS via https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9127976/efx-maintains-rating-by-rbc-capital-price-target-lowered-to-177

findings.finding: Equifax issued $1bn of senior notes (5.000% 2029, 5.650% 2033) on 29 Jul 2026 to repay commercial paper, and Círculo de Crédito ($750m EV) is expected to close in Q4 2026. The financing term-outs existing CP and pre-funds the acquisition, and is not distress; 2H buybacks continue at a slower pace with leverage below 3x.
findings.why_not_priced: Asked what the money buys: CP refinancing and acquisition capacity, so the sign is zero. At most a few cents of interest drag in the Q4 guide with the Fed hiking, plus a possible reported-revenue add from Círculo if it closes in Q4.
findings.independence: Círculo close timing from the Q2 release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000033185/000003318526000024/exhibit99120260630.htm

findings.finding: A $100m class settlement over the 2022 'OMS' credit-score coding error got preliminary approval on 17 Aug 2026 (final hearing 22 Jan 2027). It will likely appear as a legal charge excluded from adjusted EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Legal charges are excluded from adjusted EPS and have not moved EFX prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since August, about $0.65/share pre-tax GAAP and below the adjusted line, with no path to the guide; sized at a fraction.

outside_window.finding: A formal FHFA tri-merge to bi-merge directive for Fannie/Freddie deliveries ('within weeks' per Bloomberg; Pulte skipped the MBA Annual slot). Timing is undated and unlikely to land exactly in the 20 Oct session; William Blair puts EFX tri-merge-linked revenue at ~$270m.
Medicaid/SNAP work requirements take effect Jan 2027, with more frequent Work Number checks: a 2027 revenue driver for EWS government.
TransUnion Q3 2026 print, expected after EFX, gives a peer read on mortgage inquiries; it lands after the exit window.

baseline_tension: The negative lean agrees with the skew (+2.58, downside paid, P/C OI 1.95) and runs against the +8.4% five-day bounce. Agreement with the skew means part of it is priced, which moved p_up from 40 to 42. The run-up is a sector relief rally with no company news, which is why the negative is not shrunk further.
lessons_applied: Lesson 9 (segment net of rest): Q3 mortgage proxy finding cut from -1.0 to -0.8, because mortgage is about a quarter of revenue and EWS/International/cost levers can offset.
Lesson 6 (bar): the FY consensus $8.53 under the Q4-guide finding is single-source and possibly stale, so that finding was capped from -1.8 to -1.5.
Lesson 5 (proxy): hiring macro finding cut from -0.4 to -0.3, since Talent decline was already in the Q2 guide.
Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sells beats): beat-track/AI-savings finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the $1bn notes refinance CP and pre-fund Círculo, so that finding went from -0.1 to 0.0 and was merged with the Círculo item (0.0), one finding instead of two.
Lesson 3 (read the set): the PT-cut reset finding (+0.4) and the guide-cut finding conflict partly; resolved by keeping both net and trimming the PT finding to +0.3.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest checked at ~6% float, 3-4.6 days to cover, not crowded, so no squeeze shrink; skew agrees with the sign, so p_up moved 40 to 42, abs_move left at 7.5.
